title: Kaliya

segments.voice: Yesterday, maya: Yashoda saw everything, then was given back her ordinary love. Your line was the forgetting is the gift.

A hot day by the Yamuna. The boy Krishna is old enough now to take the calves and cows out to graze with his friends. It's summer, and on this day Balarama isn't with them. Desperate with thirst, the boys and the cattle come down to a part of the river and drink, and drop where they stand, cowherds and cows alike, lifeless at the water's edge. Krishna looks at them, the text says, with a glance full of nectar, and they get up, puzzled, as if waking from sleep. Something is wrong with that water.
screen: `A HOT DAY BY THE YAMUNA.` → `THEY DRINK, AND FALL.` → `A GLANCE BRINGS THEM BACK.`

segments.voice: What's wrong is Kaliya. In a deep pool of the Yamuna lives a great serpent, a naga with many hoods, whose poison has turned the pool boiling and deadly. The Bhagavata says birds flying over it fall out of the sky. The plants on its banks are dead. Krishna decides the river has to be made clean again. He climbs a tall kadamba tree on the bank, tightens his clothes, slaps his arms like a wrestler, and jumps right into the poisoned pool. The water heaves. Kaliya rises, furious that someone has entered his home. He sees a small, dark, beautiful boy playing in the water, bites him, and wraps him in his coils. And Krishna goes still. Up in the village, people see terrible omens and look for Krishna, and he isn't there. Everyone runs to the river: the women, the old men, the children, the cows. They follow his footprints to the bank and see him, motionless, wrapped in a serpent. Yashoda wants to go into the water after him. Nanda does too. The gopis cling to her, grieving. One person on that bank is calm. Balarama, the text says, knows his brother's power, and he holds them back, and smiles. So the chapter leaves us in a strange place: a whole village in despair on the bank, one brother quietly smiling, and in the water, the boy they love, perfectly still, inside the coils.
screen: `A POISONED POOL IN THE YAMUNA.` · `HE JUMPS FROM THE KADAMBA TREE.` · `THE WHOLE VILLAGE RUNS TO THE BANK.` · then, large: `BALARAMA SMILES.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind something you're watching from the bank right now: someone you love in a hard place, a situation you can't jump into and fix. Breathe with the worry honestly, then let in a little of Balarama's calm, the possibility that more is happening in the water than you can see, and hold both. If you pray, you can hold that person in prayer.
Kaliya. The many-hooded serpent whose poison fills a pool of the Yamuna, and who wraps the boy Krishna in his coils.
Your line: still in the coils. Tomorrow, the boy in the river gets up. See you then.

howItsDone: Pilgrims in Vrindavan visit a bathing place on the Yamuna associated with Kaliya, and some festivals reenact the boy Krishna's leap into the river.

chat.says: Why was Balarama smiling while everyone else panicked at the river?
options: He knew his brother's power, so he held the others back, calm.
He hadn't seen the serpent yet and thought Krishna was swimming.
He thought the village was overreacting to one of Krishna's games.
chat.meaning: The text says Balarama knew Krishna's power. While the village despaired on the bank, he held them back, and smiled.

Kaliya.meaning: a many-hooded serpent poisoning a pool of the Yamuna

naga.meaning: a serpent being, often with many hoods

kadamba.meaning: a tall tree on the Yamuna's bank

Yamuna.meaning: the river where the cowherds graze their herds
